utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you also see a date on the document, that is, 6 May 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign that document on that date?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the same date, did you indicate where you, Mr. Franjic, and Mr. Vucic were when the shooting occurred?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you place a cross on the map with a red pen to indicate your approximate position at the time of the shooting?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. Yes, I did, but it should be moved a little to the left, because Sinjevo is marked on the road, and the pavement is where we were actually walking down, not in the middle of the road. We were walking down the pavement, so it should be moved a little to the left if you look towards Dobrinja, in the direction of Dobrinja. A little to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a pointer that you can use to point to the map? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to show you? What I mean is, you should move this to the left-hand side, to the pavement. It should be moved about 2 metres to the left. That would be the exact point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, I think you said that at the time of the shooting, you and the other two gentlemen were walking on Ante Babica Street. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please point to Ante Babica Street.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Here it is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the map could be adjusted on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please point again to Ante Babica Street.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness indicates the area of the cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, could you please point to the area of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And could the ELMO please be zoomed back so that we can see more of the map.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be a better -- perhaps it would be better if there was a photograph. Then I would be able to make my way round it better, because this is a large area. It's difficult for me to find my way on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. In that case, Mr. Kapetanovic, I will not ask you any more questions about the map. Mr. President, I ask that we now see a video, being Prosecution Exhibit 3280U.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, perhaps before doing that, could we indicate for the transcript what I think I saw. That is to say that when the witness was asked where Ante Babica Street was, he made a gesture with his hand going to the right of the cross marked in red, and he showed this direction; he indicated this direction with this gesture of his hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would agree with that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's then in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps Ms. Philpott could confirm, when the video starts playing, that it is visible to the witness in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please do so, Ms. Philpott.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] I'll do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, please look at the computer screen in front of you, and shortly you should see a video. Please watch the video and listen carefully.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video is beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unfortunately, we --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just ask the technical booth not only to provide Sarajevo with the image but also The Hague. Mr. Kapetanovic, you were able to see a video, we were not, so we'll try restart the video that we all can see it. May I ask the technical booth whether this is a serious problem or that we could expect to have the image on our screens soon? Mr. Kapetanovic, you still have -- you need some patience, as we have to have some patience as well. Could I be informed about what the problem is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm informed that it might take another minute to solve the problem. What would you prefer to do, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps I can ask a few more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If the technical booth would just inform the registrar as soon as the problem seems to be solved. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, what ethnic community did you belong to or do you belong to?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: A Catholic, a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Mr. Franjic? What was his ethnic grouping, if I could put it that way?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The same as me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: And Vucic too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've told us that you believe that the shooting came from your right. Whereabouts was the confrontation line on that day in relation to where you were shot? How far away was it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Two hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From where you were shot, was it possible to see any buildings on the other side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: There was the students' hostel and two private houses which were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which side of the confrontation line was the student hostel on, or was it in the middle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I would like to make the following observation: The question posed by Mr. Ierace began as follows: [In English] "From where you were shot ..." [Interpretation] It doesn't seem to me to be possible to determine what Mr. Ierace -- what precise point Mr. Ierace was making starting out with that phrase, that is to say, the point where he was shot or the point from which he was targeted, he was shot at. This would make a difference with respect to the side of the line, and I don't think it is precise enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you are objecting and commenting to the question at the same time. Would you please limit yourself next time in making the objection, saying that the point Mr. Ierace points at is not clear. That would be enough, without further explanation, until we ask for that. Mr. Ierace, could you please rephrase your question in such a way that whatever confusion would be there is avoided.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, you've told us that the bullet hit the three of you, bullet or bullets hit the three of you, although in your case it hit your clothing, not your body. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which forces controlled the area where you and your friends were when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: That was the area which was not under occupation. It was not occupied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean by that the forces of the Bosnian government?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which force or forces, as you understood it, controlled the other side of the confrontation line closest to where you were shot?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The Serb forces held it, the front. That's where the front was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you formed the opinion that the shot came from your right, and you were walking towards Dobrinja at the time that the three of you were shot. What area was on your right that you could see from that position?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It was the home for the blind that is, we assume, the bullet or bullets came from, and we didn't hear the sound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which force or forces controlled the area where the home for the blind was on that date?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you assume that the bullet or bullets were fired from the home for the blind?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the shot, the way that the two of them were shot, Ivan and Vucic, because they were on the right-hand side. We thought that the bullet or bullets came from our right, from the direction of the blind children's home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I was informed that the technical problem has been solved.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I understand you to be saying that the position of the entry wounds on Ivan and Augustin led you to the conclusion that the bullet came from your right as you faced Dobrinja. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps at this stage we could see the video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, we will try again to show the video so we can see it here and in Sarajevo as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Philpott, could you confirm that it --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] We are able to see the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Could you please point, to the best of your recollection, in the direction from which you and your friends were walking on the day that the shooting took place. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates]. "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Could you please point in the direction that you were walking, to the best of your recollection, on that day. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates]. "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Can you please stand in the spot where, to the best of your recollection, you were located when the shooting occurred. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates]. "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: I will now mark that spot with yellow spray paint in the figure X on the sidewalk. "Can you please indicate with your hand where your friends Ivan and Augustin were located in relation to you when the shooting occurred, to the best of your recollection. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates]."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, did you recognise yourself in the video that you just saw?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you carry out the directions of the investigator truthfully to the best of your recollection on the video?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, in a moment you will see a photograph on your screen. Would you please tell us when you can see the photograph. Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness's answer could be translated.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We did not hear any answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that response, Mr. Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: What I see before me, the President of the Court or of the Chamber. That is what I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps Ms. Philpott could assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Philpott, could you please assist in--

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- putting a photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] We cannot see anything other than Mr. Ierace, and now yourself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace. What photo are we supposed to see?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it is P3279U, and the image is an intersection with traffic lights.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps we need the assistance of the technical booth to send the signal through from my case manager's computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on your computer. It's your case manager's computer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would expect it, then, on the computer evidence, but that gives a totally different picture. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you. I merely wanted to seize the opportunity of this technical glitch to say that the investigator is asking the witness in the video "Where were your friends?" Could Mr. Ierace tell us where in the testimony the witness said that these two people were his friends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I don't think it's necessary to have this clarified. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, can you now see a photograph of an intersection on the screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Mr. Ierace, are you playing the Quicktime movie?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, it should be on the "Computer Evidence" button, if you have such a button.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] We do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It is the same type of material which was shown to the first videolink witness, if that assists in locating the appropriate button.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] We do now see an image, however it's not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Mr. President, perhaps I could ask some more questions whilst the technical booth can try and improve the problem. A shrug of the shoulders through the glass suggests that nothing more can be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what is the reason for the unclarity reported to us by Sarajevo, but if the technicians could please see what's the best way of doing it. I see that there's a -- there's a new CD-rom here, so it could be played perhaps from the technical booth. No, it's usually played from the Prosecution computer. Could the technical booth please try to find out what causes the unclarity. And may I ask again to Ms. Philpott, is it still unclear?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I suggest that we give the technical operator our copy of the CD, and he could experiment within the technical booth perhaps whilst I ask some more questions and show some photographs through the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed in that way. I don't know how it was done last time when we had the 360-degrees photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That was done from the bar table operated by the case manager, and it apparently worked with the first videolink witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed, and let's see whether the technicians could solve the problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, before you saw the video, I was asking you some questions about your opinion that the bullet or bullets came from your right, and you explained that your reasoning was based partly on the places that you and your friends were shot. Earlier, you said that Augustin Vucic was wounded on his left-hand side. Which way was he facing at the time that he was shot?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: In the direction in which we were moving, towards Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to -- perhaps you could tell us in more detail which part of his body bore a wound.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Vucic, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The left side of his body, where his heart and his kidneys are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the bullet came from the right, how was it that the left-hand side of his body was injured or wounded?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to -- he was slightly shorter than Franjic, and therefore it got him in the stomach, above the belly button, and he was hit in his left side. Now, of course, I do not know whether it was one or two bullets. I can't really say that. But that is the gist of what I am trying to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it from that last answer that the entry point appeared to you to be in the stomach, above the belly button. Is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. Quite so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you also mean that the wound extended from that point to the left side?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I think, at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that Exhibit P3279OA be placed on the ELMO and a copy of that photograph be shown to the witness in Sarajevo. This is a photograph that was tendered into evidence through Fuad Dziho. Mr. President, I'm not able to see the photograph on the video evidence button at the moment. I wonder if that's because the technical booth is experimenting with that channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It might be. I see the photograph on video, and that's, I would say, the Sarajevo copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. I heard from the French booth that they did not hear the last name, so could it be please repeated so that we could also hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What last name are you referring to, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? The witness with whom the photograph was tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The name of the witness for whom this photograph -- to whom this photograph was shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness Dziho, which is written D-Z-I-H-O. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, I think you have in front of you a photograph which shows a view from above of some buildings and some streets. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise what appears in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems that we are not getting the photograph on our screen. We are trying, but -- oh, yes. Oh, yes, now we have it. Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what it is that appears in the photograph that you recognise. Mr. Kapetanovic, I'll ask you that question again. Would you please tell us what you recognise in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I see two buildings near the students' hostel from which we believe the bullet came which hit us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, would you please point with your pen to the student hostel. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The student hostel is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the transcript, the witness points to the high-rise building at the top centre of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please point to the buildings that you described as "the two buildings near the students' hostel from which we believe the bullet came which hit us."

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness indicates two buildings in the centre of the photograph, that is, in front of the high-rise building, the first being a white building with some red writing on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please point to the second building again, Mr. Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And the second building being behind and to the left of the white building with the red writing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, do you see that in front of the white building with the red writing there is a building of light-brown brick with a white band and a red roof? If so, could you please point to that building.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness points to a building so described in the dead centre of the photograph. Now, I ask that Ms. Philpott place on the ELMO in Sarajevo photograph Exhibit P3265.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, we're now going to change the photographs, but the photograph that you're presently pointing to, could you leave that on the desk in front of you so that you can compare two photographs. Mr. Kapetanovic, do you recognise the photograph that's in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you place the black marks on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm pointing at it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you put those black marks on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, does your signature appear on the photograph in the area of the sky?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you mean to indicate by the black marks on the buildings to which you are now pointing?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the transcript, that is the light-red roof area.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I marked it because we thought that it was between the student hostel and this building, and these buildings is where the bullet was fired from, the direction from which we believe we were hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've marked the roof area of those two buildings, that is, the white building with the red writing and the -- withdraw that. You've marked a light red roof area in the photograph. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please compare that photograph to the one that you looked at previously, which, for the transcript, is P3279OA. I want you in particular to compare firstly a building painted white with the red lettering. Do you see that on both photographs?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you also see on both photographs a building which is constructed of light brown bricks with a whitish band towards the top of the wall, and above it a red roof? Do you see that building on both photographs?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now direct your attention to the photograph on which you placed some black lines on the roofs. Are you looking at that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't really see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you see the photograph on which you placed your signature with a black pen?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you placed your signature on that photograph, did you also put some lines on the roofs of the two buildings with a black pen?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't draw it unless -- I mean, I was pointing at it, what was destroyed, which houses were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. At the time that you and the other two men were shot, did those two buildings exist?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: One was standing. The other one was already destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which one was standing, the white one or the light brown one?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The white one, and this light brown was destroyed. I mean its roof was gone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the white one have its roof on the day that you and the other two men were shot?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No, it didn't. It didn't, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you sign this photograph in September of last year?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. President. For the transcript, I do not know if that is the same thing. But personally, I see two buildings which are white and which have red lettering on them, and which both have roofs. One is in the centre of the photograph, and the other one I would say is right behind it. So for the sake of clarity, could we make it more precise for the transcript. The witness said two buildings, but I see here two buildings which are both white.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Both white, Mr. President, but not both with red roofs. I'm happy to clarify it if my friend is unclear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's clear to the Chamber, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kapetanovic, did you sign this photograph at around the same time that you participated in the video that we saw a short time ago?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that in approximately September of last year?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say that officially, but that is my guess. I cannot really officially confirm it, whether it was September, the end of it or early September. I don't really know. But I signed it, because -- and I did the statement which I gave about the incident. And on the basis of that, I signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So we now understand that the significance of the lines on the red roofs is that those red roofs were not there on the day that you and your the other two men were shot. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the French transcript, it is not red lines; it is the red roof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, therefore, on that day, if one were standing in the position of the camera that took this photograph, it was possible to see beyond those red roofs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Behind the red roofs was the students' hostel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the left of the students' hostel, one could see whatever was behind there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Assuming that you could see, because the students' hostel was on the right-hand side as you moved towards the blind people's home, and on the left-hand side were the residential blocks, several storeys high. And here you could see to the blind people's home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to ask you some questions about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, before you touch a new area, I think it would be time to have a break, if this would be a suitable moment. Yes. Mr. Kapetanovic, we are going to have a break for 20 minutes. So we hope to see you on the screen again after 20 minutes. We'll adjourn until 5 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Philpott, could you please escort the witness back in the videoroom. And as far as I understand, Mr. Ierace, all the technical problems have been resolved. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I perhaps first ask Ms. Philpott to confirm the quality of the computer evidence picture. Ms. Philpott, could you confirm that it's well visible?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Yes, much better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, shortly -- first of all, do you have in front of you a photograph?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Do I have what? Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please assume from me that this photograph is taken from the position that you indicated on the video as the position you were in --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- when the three of you were shot. All right. We will now move the photograph to the left. Do you recognise now towards the middle of the image the building you identified earlier as the student hostel?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, having regard to your earlier evidence, were the two buildings which you have identified as being in front of the student hostel behind the traffic which appears in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are we now looking up Ante Babica Street in the direction of Dobrinja, having regard to your earlier evidence?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, we now see the direction in which you and the other two men were walking at the time that the three of you were shot?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can still see on this image part of the student hostel, that is, on the right-hand side of the screen, above the yellow truck; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the day you were shot, was the student hostel in the same condition in which it appears in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I should explain. By "condition," I mean was it in any way damaged in 1994, at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was damaged on the inside; that is to say, it was all destroyed inside. But as far as the building is concerned, it remained standing, the same, status quo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it possible to see through any part of the building in 1994?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Through what parts of the building could you see in 1994?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: You could see through the windows, towards the front. You could see through the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the building have any glass in its windows in 1994?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No, it didn't. No, it wasn't repaired. It was only later on that the repairs began, after 1994, 1995, 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll now continue to move the photograph to the left. We now see a building in reddish-brown brick on the left of the photograph. Was that building there on the day that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We continue to move the photograph to the left and we stop where we started. Thank you for looking at that, Mr. Kapetanovic. I'd now like to take you back to the two photographs that I showed you earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps Ms. Philpott could place the two photographs in front of the witness. They are Exhibits P3279OA and P3265. I draw your attention in particular to P3265. Perhaps Ms. Philpott could place in photograph on the ELMO in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, it appears that you also placed some black lines on the student hostel in September of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, but probably when it was taken, these lines were placed there. And it is assumed that that's where the shooting -- that the shooting took place there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I do apologise. But yes, we were speaking about the other buildings later on. I think I heard the witness say that he himself did not make those black lines on any of the buildings. At least, as far as the two front buildings are concerned, he said that he didn't place the black lines there. So Mr. Ierace's question seems to me to be inexact in respect of what the witness himself said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, would you please respond. My recollection -- well, let's not talk about my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, so as to avoid any doubt as to the issue, I will clarify. Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you perhaps assist us, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. You say that the witness said that he didn't place the black lines there. Could you indicate where he said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. That was my recollection, but I will check it out willingly. If the Prosecution hasn't found it, I'll do it myself. Quite willing to. I was following the Serbian. That's why the English transcript, I don't know if it says the same thing, but I'll check it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could, whatever is in the transcript at this very moment, perhaps clarify the issue, Mr. Ierace, or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Page 59, line 12. Line 11 says: "Did you put those black marks on that photograph?" The answer is: "Yes, I did."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please then proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have a technical problem. My colleague and General Galic said that he didn't say that in Serbian. Now, I will check what the transcript says, and perhaps we can come back to that point of what was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you think, on the basis of your research of the original tape, that the transcript should be changed, of course we'll be glad to pay proper attention to that. On the other hand, you'll understand that we cannot find it out right away, so please come back to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll approach the issue from a different direction. I ask that a document be placed on the ELMO, identified as "Statement" at this stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, please look on your computer screen and tell me if you see a typed document.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the document be moved up the screen so that we can see the bottom of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise on the screen your signature?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I recognise it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you also see on the screen a date?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I see it, the 25th of the 9th, 2001. 25th of September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you write that date? Is the date in your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you place your signature and the date on this document as a means of confirming the contents of a document as read --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- as read and translated to you on that date as being correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the statement is only six lines long. My learned colleagues have a copy. I propose to read the statement to the witness; the relevance of it is to refresh his memory as to the reason he made the marks on the photograph which I anticipate were made on the same date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace. And perhaps you read slowly since I must assume that the interpreters' booths have no translation at this -- no copy of it at this moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, I'm going to read to you the contents of that statement made by you on the 25th of September, 2001, to an investigator of the Prosecutor's office. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I will now read the statement. "Further to my previous statements, today investigator Jonathan Tait-Harris has shown me a photograph that shows the area of the scene of the incident about which I have made a witness statement. I have marked upon the photograph the parts of buildings that were destroyed or damaged to such an extent that they allowed a far greater field of view. I confirm that the photograph is an accurate representation of the scene. As such, I have endorsed the photograph with my signature and today's date." That completes your statement. Mr. Kapetanovic, does that remind you of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise for intervening, but what I see of the statement is that the witness is declaring that he covered the photograph with his signature, and I am going to quote, and it is today's date. On the document that we're talking about, I do not see any date whatsoever, Mr. President, which once again poses the problem of document authenticity. All I see is the possible signature of the witness and nothing else. I don't know if Mr. Ierace can show me the date on his own document, where it is. Because on my document, Mr. Ierace, I don't see any date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I agree that the photograph does not bear a date, but the witness has not disputed and, as I understood it, until that moment, the Defence has not disputed that this was the photograph indeed signed by the witness. The witness has given evidence already that he signed this photograph at about the same time as he cooperated in the making of the video in approximately September of last year. Therefore, although the photograph does not bear a date, in my submission, that does not preclude the Prosecution from proceeding on the basis consistent with the witness's evidence that this is indeed the photograph referred to in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I ask you what specific interest you have in knowing the date of the picture? I mean, the testimony seems to be quite clear that this is not a picture which reflects the situation at the time of the incident. Is it that you -- so I think -- I don't know whether you could agree on that together with the Prosecution. So if you could agree on that, I'd like then to know what is the specific reason why you'd like to know what date, if not the date of the incident, the photograph is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Let me say that I'm completely indifferent to the date. It doesn't matter to me. What I'm not indifferent to is the fact that this witness, in a statement that has just been quoted by the mouth of Mr. Ierace, he said that on the document he recognises the reality of the scene, the exact scene, and to confirm it. He placed two things on the document: One was his signature and the second point was the date on that day. So necessarily we seem to be speaking about a different document, and this document, or at least one of the two -- does not have one of the two observations of the witness; that is to say, it does not include both the signature and the date. So I would like to know where is the document that the Prosecution refers to? Because there must be another document, according to the witness, which should have, written in his own handwriting, both his signature and the date on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now better understand your objection. Mr. Ierace, could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, clearly it is an oversight that the date is not on the photograph. In saying that, I also rely on the ERN numbers of the statement and the photograph. The statement commences with ERN 0211-4232. The last page of the statement, that is, the written part of the statement, is 0211-4235. The ERN of the photograph is 0211-4236. In other words, this photograph formed part of that statement at the time that it was processed by the Evidence Unit. Mr. President, I also seek to ask a further question or two of the witness, since this has become an issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- do you still have in front of you the photograph that bears your signature in the area of the sky?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first give the opportunity to Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I'm not quite sure that I fully grasped what the Prosecution said with these figures. It is, however, very important that we know whether this first statement which was given by the statement [as interpreted] conforms with this so that we can see quite clearly so as to know this type of photograph. Otherwise the conclusion is obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just see whether Mr. Ierace, in putting questions to the witness, could clarify the issue witness or otherwise could clarify the issue raised by you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, do you still have in front of you the photograph which has your signature on it, that is, the photograph that you signed?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the contents of your statement?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, you referred to a photograph where you marked parts of buildings that were destroyed or damaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm sorry. I'm not getting the interpretation. I cannot hear the witness answering, and this is already the third question that my learned friend is asking. And General Galic also tells me that he cannot hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's just first check on whether the B/C/S audio channel gives a signal. Could you please speak a few words, Mr. Kapetanovic, since we have difficulties in receiving your voice in the original language. Just count to ten. That will do. Ms. Philpott, could you please assist us in asking the witness to speak a few words in his own language so that we can see whether the audio is functioning well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you well. I don't know whether there is some other problem, but I can hear very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We confirm that there is an improvement. We now hear what the witness is saying in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, since some of us could not hear your answers to a couple of questions, I expect Mr. Ierace to take you back a few questions, and would you then please answer perhaps the same questions again so that we all can hear your answers. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, do you still have in front of you the photograph that you signed?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the contents of your statement dated the 25th of September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I do remember certain things. I don't remember others. It was read to me at that time, and I know what I stated, what I will state now again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the statement, you referred to a photograph on which you marked parts of buildings that were destroyed or damaged. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which photograph was that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: This photograph with my full name on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "full name," do you mean your signature on it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: And signature, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps Ms. Philpott could place that photograph that the witness is referring to on the ELMO so that we can see it in The Hague. Thank you. For the record, that is Photograph Exhibit Number P3265.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Kapetanovic, the marks that you placed on the student hostel were to indicate that it was destroyed or damaged so that there was a far greater field of view. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now look at Photograph P3279OA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can the witness be asked to tell us what the date was, because he seems to remember the date -- the time of the statement, and perhaps he will remember the time of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, of course you may ask these questions when cross-examining the witness. I don't think that there's any necessity at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you now have in front of you photograph -- I'll withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps Ms. Philpott can place that photograph on the ELMO in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is, as far as I can see, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kapetanovic, we saw you indicate a position on the footpath of Ante Babica Street where you and the other two men were when the three of you were shot. Do you see in this photograph that part of the footpath where you were standing at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please point to it with your pen.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps the ELMO could zoom back.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, for the benefit of the transcript, the witness indicates a position to the left of the photograph where two pedestrian crossings would meet up if extended. It is approximately in the position of what appears to be a box on the footpath with two footpaths radiating from the box.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, do you remember that when we saw the photograph on the screen taken from the position where you were shot, there was a building very close by with dark brick?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm sorry. I'm trying to be as precise as possible. The description by Mr. Ierace in English describes the zone where two pedestrians were crossing, and I must confess that I do not see anyone crossing, but there are several pedestrians. So could Mr. Ierace be more accurate in his description.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think Mr. Ierace was referring to pedestrian crossings, which is where pedestrians cross the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the interest of saving time, I'll ask the witness to mark the position. That should overcome my friend's objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To mark it. Isn't it an exhibit that has already been entered into evidence, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I correct myself, Mr. President. You're quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, I think it was quite clear. I'm very grateful for Mr. Piletta-Zanin if he assists us in explaining to us what is unclear in the English text. But I think that this was not necessary and would suggest a better understanding of the English language before doing so. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, marking could be done if there is an extra copy available in Sarajevo, of course. I wouldn't prevent you from marking, but not on the -- I think the original might be here, and then Ms. Philpott would have to take the marked copy from Sarajevo to The Hague. And it should be given then another number. That would be possible, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps I can describe the position in a different way that would remove my friend's doubt. The position indicated by the witness was to the left of the photograph in the vicinity of the intersection of the four-lane road which appears across the bottom of the photograph and a road that extends parallel to the side of the photograph, to the left of a red vehicle on the intersection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, do you remember that a short while ago, I showed you a photograph on the computer screen taken from where you indicated you and the other two men were shot. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you also remember that we moved the photograph around in a circle, and you pointed out certain things as we moved around the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that there was a small building with dark-coloured bricks very close to that position, and you said that building was there at the time that the three of you were shot?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right, but there was a building further away which was shown. This building was built later on, that I mentioned earlier. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: There was a store there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, I will show you again the electronic photograph. Please watch your screen and tell us when you can see it. Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] Your Honour, we do not have the photograph on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you, Ms. Philpott, confirm to us as soon as you have the 360-degrees photograph on your screen in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Sarajevo] We now have the image on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, do you see on the screen in front of you a high-rise white building to the left?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that building there on the day that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that the first two floors, approximately, appear to be a light-blue colour?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will move the photograph slightly to the left. Do you see that in front of the building, that is, between the camera and the white building, there is a building with a red roof which consists of just a ground level?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look again at the photograph taken from above and place that -- I think -- and place that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps Ms. Philpott could do that. For the record, that's P3279OA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you please look to the right of that photograph. Move your pen to the right edge of the photograph. Mr. Kapetanovic, could you please move your pen to the right edge of the photograph. Mr. Kapetanovic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please move your pen to the right of the photograph. Please move it to the right edge of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not to the right edge of the building but to the right edge of the photograph itself, Mr. Kapetanovic, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Kapetanovic --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Here, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, on the right edge of the photograph, do you see a high-rise building which is white and the first two floors or so are blue, that is, the top right-hand corner of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I think you are now pointing at that building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you remember on the electronic photograph I pointed out another building in between the camera and the high-rise building which has a red roof and it is just the ground floor? Do you see that photograph -- I'm sorry. Do you see that building in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you now pointing at that building?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the record, the witness -- perhaps we could have the ELMO back again. The witness is pointing --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please put your pointer back on that building, Mr. Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the record, the witness is pointing at a building with a red roof which appears on the extreme right-hand side of the photograph, slightly below centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you remember that on the electronic photograph, that building that you're now pointing at was in the same line of sight, as seen from where you were shot, as the white high-rise building behind it? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now go -- look again at the photograph to which you were pointing. That's Exhibit P3279OA. And can you see on the photograph in front of you the corner --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now see in that photograph the part of the footpath where you were standing when you and the other two men were shot?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I can see part of the pavement, but I do not see the exact spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now look again at the electronic photograph, which we will move to the right. Let me know when you can see the electronic photograph on the screen. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... as we move the photograph slowly to the right. Do you see that a short distance in front of the camera there is a side street? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We will now continue to move the photograph to the right. Do you see that there is a building almost on that intersection, that is, it would seem, a matter of a few --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- a matter of a few metres from where you were shot? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please wait for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, meanwhile, my apologies to the Chamber and the Prosecution for my last intervention. I wasn't -- I really misheard. I didn't quite get what Mr. Ierace was saying. But I accept the ruling of the Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we will continue moving the photograph slightly to the right, and please look at the roof of that small building as we do so. All right. Now, please look again at the photograph, that is, photograph --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could have on the screen the photograph on the ELMO in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you see, on the bottom right-hand corner of the photograph, in the very bottom of the right-hand corner of the photograph, there is a pedestrian crossing? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please point to it. Please point to the pedestrian crossing in the bottom right-hand corner, further to the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the right. Further to the right and to the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You are now pointing -- please place your pointer back on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And please leave your pointer there for a moment. You are now pointing at the pedestrian crossing which appears in the bottom right-hand corner of the photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you see that immediately to the left of that pedestrian crossing, one can see part of a roof, a flat brown roof? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one can see a person standing on the footpath alongside that roof. Do you see that person?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, not all that well really. But...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please point to the roof.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Would you bring your pointer back down to the bottom right-hand corner of the photograph. Please take your pointer back to where it was before in the bottom right-hand corner of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The red house or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. Please take it to where you had it just a moment ago at the bottom of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you see that perhaps a centimetre to the left of your pen tip, there is a person standing on the footpath?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Underneath your pen tip, do you see a person standing on the footpath?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that there appears to be a brown flat roof alongside the person? Underneath your pen.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness now points --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, having regard to the electronic photograph, in particular, the position of the high-rise white building, the red roofed one-floor building, and the dark-brown small building immediately alongside where you were when you were shot, does it follow that you were standing on the footpath --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: In the direction on the crossing towards the end of the road where there is the pedestrian crossing, and we were on the road facing the structures that were photographed, those three buildings. That is the direction that we were moving to, being 10, 15 metres, perhaps even less than that, away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If I can put it to you another way, do you see the person standing alongside the roof? Please point to that person again.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that approximately where you were -- no. Can you bring the pointer back down to the flat brown roof.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that approximately where you were standing when you and the other two men were shot?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you accurately point out the position where you were standing when you and the other two men were shot to the investigator --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, but only for the transcript, it is quite possible that the clear -- the answer of the witness is no, but it is rendered at the moment we could not hear because the counsel was not speaking into the microphone indicating then two pedestrian crossings in front of this small structure which the Prosecution described as a brownish colour. And the answer of the witness was "no." And it is where the two pedestrian crossing meet and where there is a white car and in front of a brownish building which was described by the Prosecution as having the roof of that colour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Ierace, I think I'd better interfere. Mr. Kapetanovic, you have seen a video before. You also have seen a picture that was moving in all directions. You then indicated where you were standing when two men accompanying were shot, were shot at. At this video, did you indicate precisely where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did the other photograph which you could look in all directions indicate also the position where you were at that time, and was that the position from which you could look around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, it's ten minutes -- it's five minutes to 2.00 now. I don't know whether this would be a suitable moment to interrupt your examination-in-chief. Could you indicate how much time you'd still need? Because I am aware of the problems you're having as far as the speed is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Although I only have about five minutes to go, I think that in terms of reliability, the witness would benefit from a break. I'd be grateful if I could do those five minutes tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps that's wiser to do. Mr. Kapetanovic, the counsel for the Prosecution still has a few questions for you, but since we have to take a break here, this courtroom is needed this afternoon, we'll continue tomorrow morning. Are you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you able to come back tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have to be able to so that we can finish it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm glad that you're willing to come back tomorrow morning. So we'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, but not yet. As far as I see, Mr. Kapetanovic, we expect you to be back tomorrow morning. And we'll resume at 9.00 in the time of the Hague, and Ms. Philpott will be able to tell you exactly what time it is tomorrow morning. Thank you very much for coming, and we'll see you again tomorrow morning. Ms. Philpott, the witness may be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It's clear, Mr. President, that we will not finish the evidence tomorrow. Is it possible for the videolink evidence to continue on Friday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, we have to check with the Registry whether it could be done. I assume that it will be possible. Madam Registrar, could you give us any information on that? Madam Registrar is trying to get the information. Yes, please, Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. I wanted to say something else. The Defence has absolutely nothing against it, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. obviously. But I must repeat my apologies for a moment ago, because obviously it was my mistake a moment ago, the misapprehension on my part, and therefore my fault, mea culpa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that the Chamber accepted already, in deep silence, your earlier apologies, so that's -- now we also explicitly accept it. But please be aware that if we remain silent on my apologies, that we can be considered to have accepted them. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I received a confirmation that there is no problem to continue with the videolink on Friday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
